memory_candidates: When a keyed/threaded driver has no RuleApplicationSpecCore instance, the generic driver's private *_none_saturated lemma cannot be reused directly against the keyed N-tuple stepper's findSome? shape -- re-derive it locally via List.findSome?_eq_none_iff + case-split (Phase 7's own idiom), rather than projecting through the 3-tuple generic form.

Before assuming a plan-flagged 'guard-sensitive sub-case' needs new code in the current phase, check whether an earlier landed preservation theorem already fully discharges it internally -- re-deriving may be redundant and the R1-style risk may already be isolated in already-committed code.

When a keys-threaded loop invariant (e.g. S4LoopInv.keysTotal: every known world has a recorded birth key) is designed around 'keys are assigned only at minting time', double-check the ENTRY configuration explicitly before assuming it's satisfiable: a pre-existing root world that is 'known' from its very first branch formula but never re-minted can silently violate a keysTotal-style field forever, since preservation-only proofs never need the hypothesis to be true, only implication-stable. Confirm entry satisfiability computationally (simp/lean_goal) before writing the final assembly theorem, not after.

A multi-line `simp only [...] at h1 h2 h3` tactic call, when the `at` clause's hypothesis list wraps onto a continuation line at a shallower indentation than the `simp only [...]` call itself, can produce a Lean4 parse error ('expected identifier; expected command') rather than a semantic error -- split into separate `simp only [...] at hI` calls per hypothesis instead of relying on line-wrapped `at` clauses.
